question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a certain sum at 8% per annum for 2 years is ₹144. What is the amount (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

 The difference between CI and SI for 2 years = P((r)/(100))²

Where P = Principal

r = rate

According to the trick:

C.I - S.I = P((r)/(100))²

⇒ 144 = P((8)/(100))²

⇒ 144 = P × ((8 times 8)/(100 times 100))

⇒ P = ((144 times 100 times 100)/(64))

⇒ P = 22,500

**∴ The required amount (in ₹) is 22,500.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__****Given:**

Rate =** **8% per annum

Time= 2 years

Difference between C.I and S.I = ₹144

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P times Rtimes T)/(100)

Compound Interest = P[(1 + (R)/(100))T - 1]

Where P = Principal

R = rate

T = Time

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

S.I for 2 years = (P times 8times 2)/(100)

⇒ ₹(16P)/100 ----1

C.I for 2 years = P(1+(8)/(100))² - P

 ⇒ P[(1+(8)/(100))2 - 1]

 ⇒ P[(27/25)² - 1]

 ⇒ P[(729/625) - 1]

 ⇒ P(104/625) ----2

As per the question,

Difference between C. I and S.I = ₹144 

Subtracting equation (1) by (2)

P(104/625) - 16P/100 = ₹144

⇒ P(416-400)/2500 = ₹144

⇒ 16P/2500 = ₹144

P = ₹22500

**∴ The amount (in ₹) is 22500.**
